{{Quote|I suggest we leave. It appears that Arakyd Industries manufactures its droids very well.|[[I-5YQ]]|<ref name="Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref>}}
'''Arakyd Industries''' was a major technology manufacturer, focusing mainly on [[Droid/Legends|droids]], heavy weapons, and [[Starship/Legends|starships]]. Founded by [[Veltzz Arakyd]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vulpter/Legends|Vulpter]] during the reign of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Arakyd was known for its aggressive and ruthless business strategy. A member of the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Arakyd supplied the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] with war materiel whilst also [[Spy/Legends|spying]] on them for the Republic.

After the Clone Wars, Arakyd was spared the nationalization that befell the Techno Union, and the company saw a major boost in business with the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Having acquired [[Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems]] in a hostile takeover and using their propriety technology coupled with [[Artificial intelligence/Legends|artificial intelligence]] advances, Arakyd developed the [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]]. The droid was instrumental in helping the Empire to locate the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic's]] [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]

Other major Arakyd products included the [[RA-7 protocol droid/Legends|RA-7 protocol droid]], which was used by the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] to spy on Imperial personnel; and the [[XR-85 tank droid]], which was used extensively by the Empire during [[Operation Shadow Hand]]. Following the collapse of the Empire, Arakyd underwent a change of leadership and began to work closely with the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].

==Description==
Arakyd Industries was a major manufacturing corporation, specializing in producing [[Droid/Legends|droids]], heavy weapons, and [[Starship/Legends|starships]], as well as individual starship components.<ref name="EGVV" /> Over the course of its operational history, Arakyd's products were generally designed with combat applications in mind. Although known primarily for producing droids, Arakyd's strong share in the droid market allowed the company to compete in other markets. Many of their weapons systems used integrated [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brains]] as a means to enhance their efficiency and performance.<ref name="NEGTWT" />

Arakyd focused on constructing droids with potential military applications, supplying them to groups such as the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] and [[Sector Ranger/Legends|Sector Rangers]]. By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Arakyd branched out into the commercial market.<ref name="CFTD">''[[Cynabar's Fantastic Technology: Droids]]''</ref> Many of their droids were non-[[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] in design, as the company favored functionality over appearance.<ref name="AEG Extra">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20021017web|text=''Arms & Equipment Guide'' Extras!}}</ref>

Arakyd's products were used extensively throughout the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. However, due to their military nature, many droids required certification and waivers to be purchased.<ref name="CFTD" /> Aside from its headquarters on Vulpter,<ref name="NEGTWT" /> Arakyd maintained facilities on [[Byblos/Legends|Byblos]], inhabiting [[Corporate Tower 133]],<ref name="GNN14">{{JournalCite|14|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]],<ref name="EGTD" /> and a large assembly plant on [[Kelada/Legends|Kelada]]. The Kelada plant was used to manufacture components and assemble [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bikes]] and [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcraft]].<ref name="RR" /> In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], following the success of the [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]], Arakyd bought new land on Kelada with the intention of building an assembly plant to construct the planned [[C-Viper series]], a civilian model of the Viper.<ref name="GNN14" />

==History==
===Founding and rise to prominence===
Arakyd Industries was founded on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vulpter/Legends|Vulpter]] around nine thousand [[Standard year/Legends|standard years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. The industrialist [[Veltzz Arakyd]] started the company with his children, and vowed to eliminate all of his competitors. From the beginning, Arakyd's droid models were designed for war despite strict [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] laws governing the manufacture and sale of combat automata. Arakyd used his company's well-armed droids to cow his rivals into submission, and they reluctantly agreed to become subsidiaries of Arakyd Industries. Despite amassing a large amount of wealth, Arakyd continued to employ bullying tactics to convince rival corporations to bend to the company's will.<ref name="NEGTWT" /> The company developed a reputation for ruthlessness and was known for a design philosophy that expressed menace.<ref name="NEGTD" />

Arakyd produced a range of successful exploration droids, including the [[Prowler 1000 seeker droid/Legends|Prowler 1000 exploration droid]] and the [[Vanguard probot]]. One of Arakyd's ultimate goals was to supplant [[Galalloy Industries]] as the primary manufacturer of [[Scout/Legends|scout]] droids in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. When [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] was [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY/Legends|elected]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]], Arakyd was awarded with a substantial government contract to supply Vanguard probots to the [[Republic Survey Corps/Legends|Republic Survey Corps]]. The Vanguards were put to use mapping new [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] into the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]].<ref name="NEGTD" />

===Playing both sides in the Clone Wars===
Shortly before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Arakyd joined the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] as an official member.<ref name="NEGTWT" /> Arakyd entered into a dispute with [[Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems]], claiming that the younger company's prototype [[XPLR-R]] [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]-route-mapping and habitation location unit was based off of Arakyd's own proprietary designs. The two companies entered into an eighteen-[[Standard month/Legends|month]]-long dispute, with Arakyd demanding renumeration and technology rights.<ref name="HNN50">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|50|business/1344_1.html|Sensor Technology Dispute Settled in Takeover}}</ref>

[[File:AAD-4.jpg|thumb|left|AAD assault droids during the takeover of Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems]]
Eventually, Arakyd participated in a hostile takeover of [[Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems]],<ref name="NEGTWT" /> deploying sixty [[AAD-4 assault droid]]s to take over [[Viper Tower]] in [[Hpaq]] on Vulpter. After the takeover, Arakyd kept Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems active as a research-and-development division.<ref name="HNN50" /> Now in possession of the company's propriety Viper technology,<ref name="NEGTD" /> Arakyd developed the [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]] which incorporated pioneering advances in [[Artificial intelligence/Legends|artificial intelligence]].<ref name="EGVV" />

When the Clone Wars broke out, Arakyd donated weapons, droids and equipment to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] to use in the Clone Wars, but the company made sure that their officials remained away from the conflict. As a result, they were able to retain their connections within the Republic,<ref name="NEGTWT" /> although their contracts dried up. During the war, [[Agent/Legends|Agents]] from Supreme Chancellor's inner circle approached the Arakyd [[Chief Executive Officer/Legends|CEO]] [[Hordis Boil]]. In exchange for supplying the Republic with intelligence on Techno Union [[Foreman/Legends|foreman]] [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]], the agents arranged for the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]] to purchase Arakyd products through a shell company and provide them to the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Republic's clone forces]].<ref name="NEGTD" />

In the aftermath of the Clone Wars and the defeat of the Confederacy, the Techno Union was nationalized by now-[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine and his newly established Galactic Empire. Due to their arrangement during the war, Arakyd was spared nationalization, and even inherited the assets of several liquidated Techno Union companies.<ref name="NEGTD" />

===Working with the Galactic Empire===
During the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Arakyd closely aligned itself with the galactic government and increased its reputation with several high-profile contracts with the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]].<ref name="EGVV" /> Using political manoeuvring and taking advantage of competitive infighting, Arakyd positioned itself to receive the first Imperial droid contracts,<ref name="EGTD" /> and became the Empire's primary droid manufacturer. Veltzz Arakyd continued to lead the company during this period.<ref name="NEGTWT" />

Arakyd's loyalty to the Empire was rewarded with more contracts for weapons and vehicles. Expanding their product line, Arakyd also began to produce prisoner-control equipment including [[nerve disruptor]]s and [[Interrogation droid/Legends|interrogation droids]].<ref name="NEGTWT" /> Through hard work, Arakyd became [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] primary supplier of military droids. Arakyd's models for the general consumer market were successful, but only accounted for a small percentage of the company's yearly output.<ref name="EGTD" />

In an attempt to get into the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] market, Arakyd produced the [[RA-7 protocol droid/Legends|RA-7 protocol droid]]. The rest of the droid manufacturing industry were surprised by the move when the RA-7 was unveiled at the [[North Quadrant Intergalactic Automaton Show]]<ref name="NEGTD" /> on [[Aargau/Legends|Aargau]].<ref name="Aargua/Zug">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'' states that the [[North Quadrant Intergalactic Automaton Show]] took place on Zug. {{EmailCite|email=File:EAOC discussion 2023 4.jpg|creator=Jason Fry|date=2023-10-22}}</ref> Examination of the RA-7 showed that the droid was a less than stellar design; it was cheaply assembled, the design was not aesthetic, and the cognitive module was a generation behind the current models. Arakyd's rivals could not believe that the company had produced a substandard design.<ref name="NEGTD" />

The Galactic Empire bought the entire run of RA-7 droids. Unknown to its rivals, Arakyd had no intention of selling the droid on the open market. They had produced the line at the behest of the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] to act as a [[Spy/Legends|spy]] within the Empire's own ranks. The droids were either assigned or gifted to [[Governor/Legends|governors]], [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]], and [[Officer/Legends|officers]] throughout the Empire.<ref name="NEGTD" />

[[File:Arakyd_Viper.jpg|thumb|right|A Viper probe droid on the planet Hoth]]
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Arakyd's Viper [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]] was instrumental in the Empire's discovery of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Echo Base/Legends|base]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].<ref name="EGVV" /> Arakyd continued to develop refinements of the Viper probe droid. Arakyd [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]] and Imperial [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] developed the [[Infiltrator probe droid]] at the direction of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Damon Krell]].<ref name="NEGTD" /> The success of the Viper led the company to plan a civilian model, the proposed [[C-Viper series]]. The C-Viper series was intended to operate more as a [[Security droid/Legends|security droid]] and assist in augmenting [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] security forces. The project was revealed to [[NewsNet]] [[Imperial Defense Daily]] by Arakyd representative [[Allion Vlenda]].<ref name="GNN14" />

After the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], Arakyd remained loyal to the Empire.<ref name="EGVV" /> Further advances to their [[Arakyd Probot Series|probot line]] led to the one hundred and fifty [[Meter/Legends|meter]] tall [[Hunter-Killer probot]]. It was primarily used for deep space customs inspection and blockade enforcement duties.<ref name="NEGTD" />

Arakyd also consulted with top advisors from the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] to produce the [[XR-85 tank droid]]. The first prototypes were built prior to [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn's]] [[Thrawn campaign|campaign]]. However, the experimental droid interface technology used in the unit was deemed too costly for the design to enter mass production.<ref name="EGVV" />

Imperial designers worked to refine the XR-85, and within a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] Arakyd was given the contract to mass produce the design. The droid saw extensive use during the [[Second Battle of Coruscant|Imperial reconquest]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="EGVV" />

===A new direction===
As the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] gained ascendancy, Arakyd regrouped and a new board of directors took control of the company. Despite their past allegiance, the new board of directors convinced the New Republic of its loyalty,<ref name="NEGTWT" /> although some in the government voiced objection to working with Arakyd due to their previous Imperial ties. Throwing themselves fully into working with the New Republic,<ref name="Gamer3">{{GamerCite|3|Look Sir, Droids!}}</ref> Arakyd began producing [[Security droid/Legends|security droids]], personal security devices, and legal weapons. The new products were moderately successful, although they only accounted for a small percentage of the company's annual output. Arakyd continued to work with the New Republic on new weapons and droids until the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of the extragalactic [[Yuuzhan Vong]].<ref name="NEGTWT" />

==Notable products==
===Droids===
Known primarily as a droid manufacturer, Arakyd Industries produced a number of models, usually with an eye towards exploratory or military applications.<ref name="CFTD" /> One of Arakyd's most well-known products was the [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]].<ref name="SWS">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> The Galactic Empire used Viper probe droids in their efforts to find the hidden Alliance command base during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], culminating in the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]].<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> The success of the Viper probe droid led Arakyd to develop several variants including the [[Infiltrator probe droid]] and [[Hunter-Killer probot]]. With the development of the Infiltrator, Arakyd set a precedent and their probot designs trended towards being bigger and deadlier. The Hunter-Killer design was one of the largest combat droids created, measuring one hundred and fifty meters in height and was employed as customs checkpoints and planetary blockade platforms.<ref name="NEGTD" />

[[File:Sith_probe_droid.png|thumb|left|The DRK-1 Dark Eye probe droid]]
The Viper series was not the only model of probe droid developed by Arakyd. During the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Arakyd produced the [[Vanguard probot]],<ref name="NEGTD" /> and the [[DRK-1 Dark Eye probe droid/Legends|DRK-1 Dark Eye probe droid]].<ref name="AEG">''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]''</ref> The DRK-1 was used by [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] during his hunt for [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]] when she fled [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and ended up on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> A civilian variant of the DRK-1 was produced. Lacking weaponry, it was designated as the [[DSH-3 probe droid]].<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref>

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] used<ref name="RotS">{{Film|III}}</ref> [[Prowler 1000 seeker droid/Legends|Prowler 1000 exploration droids]].<ref name="NEGTD" /> Following the execution of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Cody/Legends|Cody]] deployed Prowler 1000s to search for [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]].<ref name="RotS" /> Arakyd also manufactured the [[Spelunker probe droid/Legends|Spelunker probe droid]].<ref name="NEGTD" />

Similar to probe droids, Arakyd also produced a number of [[Survey droid/Legends|survey droids]], including the [[AS23 aerial survey droid]] which was designed to resemble an aerial predator so that local wildlife left the droid alone while surveying planets.<ref name="TUR" /> The [[6G2 DeepSpace explorer droid]] was deployed aboard [[Scout ship/Legends|scout vessels]],<ref name="RPG2ERE">''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> while the [[NR-V2 Explorer]] was developed for use by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="Gamer3" />

In addition to probe droids, Arakyd produced a number of [[Battle droid/Legends|combat droids]]. Models included the [[AZ-series battle droid]],<ref name="GaW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> and the [[AAD-4 assault droid]] which was deployed during the takeover of [[Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems]] [[Viper Tower|headquarters]] on Vulpter.<ref name="HNN50" /> Arakyd produced a number of combat models that were employed by the Empire. The [[DSK-1 "Deathstrike" seeker droid]] was an uncommon model during the Clone Wars, but production was scaled up once the Empire had been established.<ref name="UA" /> During the Clone Wars, Arakyd modified their [[Spelunker probe droid/Legends|Spelunker probe droid]], adding weapons and a [[holograph]]ic array that allowed it to blend in with the environment. Dubbed the [[Chameleon droid/Legends|Chameleon droid]], these units were deployed by the Confederacy of Independent Systems to the planet [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]].<ref name="NEGTD" />

[[File:XR-85_Coruscant.jpg|thumb|right|An XR-85 tank droid fighting on Coruscant]]
Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the [[AP-1-C attack droid]] was developed by Arakyd and was intended to be a command unit for other combat droid models deployed by the Empire.<ref name="BoC">[[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 2|''Star Wars Galaxy Magazine'' 2]]</ref> Arakyd also manufactured the [[XR-37]]<ref name="HNN50" /> and [[XR-85 tank droid]] models.<ref name="DESB">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> The XR-37 was used during Arakyd's takeover of Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems,<ref name="HNN50" /> while the XR-85 was fielded by the Empire during [[Operation Shadow Hand]].<ref name="DE">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''</ref>

Alongside their range of combat droids, Arakyd also produced several models that served in military support roles. The [[AD-series weapons maintenance droid]] was touted as being able to perform the duties of an organic armorer more efficiently. Testing showed that the droid performed only marginally better than the Empire's weapons specialists.<ref name="CFTD" /> The [[R-1 recon droid|R-1]]<ref name="FUCG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> and [[R-4 recon droid]]s were used by Imperial military forces for battlefield reconnaissance,<ref name="BPG">[[Star Wars Battlefront: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Battlefront'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> while the [[HL-444 hover loader/Legends|HL-444 hover loader]] was employed for refueling and loading [[Starship/Legends|starships]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|2|46|HL-444}}</ref>

Arakyd also manufactured a number of [[Security droid/Legends|security droids]] that were used by civilians and [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement agencies]]. The [[5-BT Threat Analysis Droid]] was used by VIPs while travelling to scan food, detect surveillance devices, and warn of possible [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]].<ref name="GoI">''[[Galaxy of Intrigue]]''</ref> Other security models included the [[BT-16 perimeter droid]],<ref name="CFTD" /> the [[G-2RD series guard droid]],<ref name="DFRSB">''[[Dark Force Rising Sourcebook]]''</ref> the [[Stiletto security droid]],<ref name="TABSB">''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]''</ref> and the [[RLG guardian droid system]].<ref name="GFT" />

Arakyd's [[EI-9 network security droid]] was designed to protect [[Computer/Legends|computer]] systems,<ref name="SGTD">''[[Scavenger's Guide to Droids]]''</ref> and the company also manufactured a number of surveillance and seeker droids to track targets. The [[FSD-6D flying surveillance droid]] was used extensively on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to keep watch on potential threats.<ref name="CoC">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/dodcampaign|text=Dawn of Defiance campaign home page}}</ref> The [[DZ-70 fugitive tracker droid]] was used to track criminals and escaped prisoners,<ref name="AEG" /> while the [[Mark VII "Inquisitor" Series Seeker Droid]]<ref name="AEG" /> and [[Mark Two seeker]] droid were employed by the Empire<ref name="CoO">''[[Choices of One]]''</ref> to track individuals of interest and interrogate or kill them.<ref name="AEG" />

[[File:RA-7_closeup.jpg|thumb|left|An RA-7 protocol droid]]
Arakyd also dabbled in the [[espionage droid]] market, producing the diminutive [[moon moth espionage droid]] designed after the [[Moon moth espionage droid|insect of the same name]].<ref name="EGTD" /> Arakyd's biggest move into the market was the [[RA-7 protocol droid/Legends|RA-7 protocol droid]] which was used by the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] to spy on the Imperial officer corps and high-ranking individuals within the Empire.<ref name="EGTD" />

At least one [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] model, the [[ACC-7 assassin droid]] was produced by Arakyd.<ref name="UA">''[[Ultimate Adversaries]]''</ref> However, the company's [[ASN courier droid/Legends|ASN courier droid]] was often refitted into assassin droids by third parties due to their ubiquity.<ref name="UA" /> The [[Seeker AS-M12 message droid|AS-M12-series messenger droid]] was another of the Arakyd's dedicated [[Courier droid/Legends|courier droids]].<ref name="SotESB">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Other droid designs included a range of [[Gladiator droid/Legends|gladiator droids]] designated as the [[Mark IX Executioner]],<ref name="BD">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20021010bloodhawk|text=Bloodhawk Down|int=Bloodhawk Down}}</ref>
the [[Mark X Executioner droid/Legends|Mark X Executioner]],<ref name="HSCS">''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''</ref> and the [[Mark XI Executioner]].<ref name="GNN3">{{JournalCite|3|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> Arakyd also produced a [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droid]], the [[PI-series medical assistant droid]].<ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

===Starships===
[[File:Helix-AJ5.png|thumb|right|The ''Helix''-class light interceptor]]
Arakyd Industries produced a number of [[Starship/Legends|starships]] during their years of operation. During the [[Jedi Civil War]], Arakyd produced the [[Lethisk-class armed freighter|''Lethisk''-class armed freighter]]. Originally intended for general commercial use, the reality was that the ship was too expensive for all but the wealthiest Republic citizens.<ref name="KOTORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> During the reign of the Galactic Empire, Arakyd produced the [[Interceptor-class light freighter|''Interceptor''-class light freighter]]<ref name="CSWE2">{{CSWECite|II|106|''Interceptor''-class light freighter}}</ref> and the [[Helix-class light interceptor|''Helix''-class light interceptor]]. The latter was a heavily armed freighter that broke the [[Bureau of Ships and Services/Legends|Bureau of Ships and Services']] armament regulations. The production of the ship was ordered to be halted by the Empire and it was mandated that existing ships have their armaments stripped down and be registered with the Imperial Security Bureau.<ref name="AJ5">{{JournalCite|5|A Buyer's Guide to Alternative Starships}}</ref>

Arakyd manufactured the [[Stellar Mag V Mining Vessel]],<ref name="Jatee">{{WEGCite|story=The Evacuation of Jatee|book=Supernova (sourcebook)}}</ref> as well as the
[[Trident-class surveyor ship|''Trident''-class surveyor ship]] which could perform in both space and underwater.<ref name="Polyhedron">{{PolyhedronCite|165|Starships of the Galaxy: Arakyd Industries Trident-class Surveyor|Starships of the Galaxy: Arakyd Industries ''Trident''-class Surveyor}}</ref>

Arakyd also produced a range of [[Hyperdrive pod/Legends|hyperdrive pods]] in order to transport their probe droids to target destinations. Two models manufactured by Arakyd were the [[Predator I]]<ref name="DFRSB" /> and the [[Probe-Mate hyperspace pod]].<ref name="GG3">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>
